title: People Ops: Hiring, Onboarding, Performance & Manager Guide (2026)
author: Aisha Patel
body:
Purpose
-------
This guide consolidates Redwood Inference's people operations standards for hiring, employee onboarding, performance and feedback cycles, and manager best practices. It is intended for hiring managers, interviewers, engineering managers, people-ops partners, and HR business partners. The goal is consistent candidate experience, predictable ramp and retention, and fair, evidence-based performance decisions.

Scope
-----
Applies to all full-time, part-time, and contractor hires at Redwood Inference across engineering, product, research, and go-to-market teams. Specific processes (e.g., executive hiring, hiring for regulated customers) may require additional steps documented in team-level playbooks.

Owner & Contacts
----------------
- People Ops (owner): people-ops@redwood.ai
- Recruiting (process owner): recruiting@redwood.ai (Greenhouse: ATS owner)
- HRIS / Payroll: hr@redwood.ai (BambooHR)
- Security & Access: infra-security@redwood.ai (Okta owner)

Key Metrics (what we track)
--------------------------
- Time-to-fill (requisition open -> accepted): target <= 45 calendar days
- Offer acceptance rate: target >= 70% (benchmarked by role band)
- Time-to-ramp (hire start -> full productivity): target median <= 90 days for ICs, 120 days for managers
- 90-day retention rate: target >= 95%
- Interview-to-offer ratio: target <= 6:1
- Candidate NPS (CSAT): target >= 8/10

1) Hiring process (standardized steps)
----------------------------------
1. Requisition & Approval
   - Hiring manager completes a requisition form in Greenhouse and attaches a role brief (1 page) including: role objective, success metrics (first 90 days), must-have skills, nice-to-have skills, salary band, and interview rubric draft.
   - People Ops verifies budget and level. Finance approval required for new headcount. SLA: People Ops response within 3 business days.

2. Job posting & sourcing
   - Recruiting posts on careers.redwood.ai, LinkedIn, and role-specific channels. Internal referrals are prioritized; referrer bonus policy applies.
   - Diverse sourcing targets required for all external roles: minimum 30% of interview slate should be underrepresented groups where possible.

3. Interview loop design and scorecard
   - Every role must have a published interview loop and a scorecard in Greenhouse. Typical loop for IC engineer: recruiter screen, technical screen (coding/system design), onsite panel (product sense, behavioral, culture add), hiring manager loop, final calibration.
   - Interviewers must use the scorecard to rate candidates (1-5) and provide written evidence tied to the rubric. Decisions are made on evidence, not intuition.

4. Interviewing best practices
   - Interviewers should meet our interviewer training requirement (annual). No single-interviewer decisions except recruiter withdraw.
   - Avoid hypothetical-only questions; prefer work-sample / system-design or take-home for senior roles. Use consistent warm-up question at start (2-3 minutes) to set candidate at ease.

5. Offer & negotiation
   - Offer package assembled by Recruiting + People Ops: base salary, equity grant, bonus target, benefits summary, start date, relocation/remote stipend if applicable.
   - Salary offers should be within published band; exceptions require VP-level approval.
   - Offer acceptance SLA: Recruiting follows up within 24 hours of offer sent; expiration typically 7 calendar days.

6. Background & reference checks
   - Background checks initiated after verbal acceptance. Standard checks: employment verification, education verification, criminal check (country-dependent). Roles with customer-facing or security-sensitive access may require enhanced screening and local compliance checks.

7. Onboarding kickoff (pre-boarding)
   - Upon acceptance, People Ops triggers pre-boarding checklist in BambooHR and creates accounts in Okta. Hiring manager receives the Pre-Board Checklist email with required tasks.

2) Employee onboarding (first 90 days)
----------------------------------
Pre-boarding tasks (completed before start date)
- Legal paperwork (I-9/E-verify or local equivalents), tax forms, benefits enrollment options.
- Equipment order: laptop, peripherals, monitor(s), VPN token. SLA: equipment ordered within 2 business days of acceptance; delivered by start date where possible.
- Access provisioning: Okta accounts, Slack, Gmail, Jira, Confluence, GitHub. Sensitive-access approvals take extra 3-5 business days per security policy.

Day 0-1 (Welcome & admin)
- Welcome email from manager with first-week agenda and a calibration of expectations.
- HR orientation: benefits overview, code of conduct, security policy overview.
- Manager schedules recurring 1:1 cadence (weekly for first 3 months).

Week 1 (set foundations)
- Team orientation: product overview, architecture primer, team goals, immediate tasks.
- Pairing sessions: onboarding buddy assigned (not the direct manager) for daily check-ins in week 1.
- Access verification: developer environment, test credentials, deployment sandbox.

30-60-90 day plan (example template)
- 30 days: complete orientation, ship first small PR/bug fix, complete required compliance training, meet key cross-functional partners.
- 60 days: own a medium-scope feature, contribute to design review, demonstrate understanding of product roadmap and codebase subsystems.
- 90 days: lead a small project end-to-end, pass ramp review with manager, and set 6-12 month career goals.

Onboarding checklist (table)
| Item | Owner | Target date | Completion |
| --- | --- | ---: | --- |
| Equipment delivered | Recruiting / Ops | Start date | - |
| Okta/Slack/Gmail access | Infra Security | Day 0 | - |
| Team intro meetings scheduled | Manager | Day 1 | - |
| 30/60/90 plan agreed | Manager & IC | Day 7 | - |

3) Performance & feedback cycles
--------------------------------
Cadence
- Continuous feedback: encouraged via 1:1s and Slack; document key feedback in Confluence or performance notes.
- Quarterly check-ins: manager provides documented written check-in summarizing progress, blockers, and goals.
- Formal cycle: annual review (calibration + compensation reviews) with optional mid-year calibration for fast-growth organizations.

Ratings & calibration
- We use a 5-point rating scale (1 Below Expectations; 3 Meets Expectations; 5 Exceeds Expectations). Calibration committees review manager-proposed ratings for IC levels and managers to ensure consistency and fairness.
- Calibration timeline: managers submit ratings two weeks prior to calibration meeting; people-ops facilitates and publishes final percentile distribution by organization.

Promotion & leveling
- Promotion criteria: evidence of sustained impact, ownership beyond current scope, and demonstrated competencies at the next level. Promotions require manager proposal, peer feedback (3-5 contributors), and a promotion packet reviewed by People Ops and the Leveling Committee.

Performance improvement plans (PIP)
- PIPs are used for structured remediation. A PIP must: define expected outcomes, list measurable success criteria, set a timeline (typically 60-90 days), and assign a PIP owner (manager + HRBP). People Ops must be looped-in before PIP issuance.

Separation & offboarding
- Voluntary: exit interview scheduled; offboarding checklist executed (revoke access, return equipment).
- Involuntary: involve People Ops and Legal; follow disciplinary policy and document evidence. Security must be notified immediately for access revocation.

4) Manager guide: one-on-ones, feedback, and difficult conversations
---------------------------------------------------------------
One-on-ones (best practices)
- Cadence: weekly 1:1s for first 3 months, then at least every 2 weeks thereafter. Timeboxed to 30-60 minutes.
- Agenda: employee-owned items first, then manager topics. Use the following recurring template:
  1. Wins & highlights
  2. Roadblocks & decisions needed
  3. Career & growth discussion
  4. Action items & commitments
- Documentation: capture notes and action items in a private Confluence page or People Ops recommended template.

Giving effective feedback
- Use evidence-based, specific examples; link to outcomes. Prefer frequent, small-course corrections over rare, large critiques.
- Follow the SBI model: Situation -> Behavior -> Impact, then desired next steps.
- When delivering critical feedback: prepare, be timely (within 3 business days of the observed behavior), and offer concrete resources/support.

Difficult conversations & escalation
- Process: attempt coaching first, document coaching steps, involve HRBP if no improvement after 2-3 coaching cycles. For serious policy violations, escalate to People Ops immediately.
- Use neutral language and document all steps. People Ops will advise on records retention and legal risk.

5) Templates, examples & snippets
--------------------------------
Interview scorecard (example)
| Competency | Target evidence | Rating 1-5 | Notes |
| --- | --- | ---: | --- |
| Technical depth | Diagnosed and fixed a production issue; explains tradeoffs | 4 | Candidate described a similar incident in detail |
| System design | Clear diagram, tradeoffs, scaling plan | 5 | Good awareness of cache & partitioning |
| Collaboration | Cross-team communication examples | 4 | Clear examples of stakeholders handled |

Sample 30-60-90 YAML snippet (manager copy/paste)
```yaml
30_days:
  goals:
    - "Complete codebase orientation and merge first PR"
    - "Meet cross-functional partners: product, infra, support"
60_days:
  goals:
    - "Own delivery of medium scope feature"
    - "Participate in design reviews"
90_days:
  goals:
    - "Lead small project end-to-end and present outcomes"
    - "Agree on career development plan"
```

Offer email subject example
- Subject: "Redwood Inference — Official Offer for Senior Software Engineer"
- Body: see Recruiting templates in Greenhouse (do not deviate on mandatory benefits language).

6) Compliance & security notes
------------------------------
- Data handling: new hires with access to customer data must complete data privacy and handling training before receiving production credentials.
- Access reviews: managers must review access lists for their team quarterly. Security will run automated audits.

7) Escalation & exceptions
--------------------------
- Fast-track hires (e.g., critical heads for customer SLAs) may use an expedited 10 business day turnaround; requires Director approval and documented business justification.
- Exceptions to diverse slate or salary bands require VP-level signoff and People Ops record.

Appendices
----------
A. Frequently asked questions (FAQ)
- Where do I find the standard offer template? -> Greenhouse / Recruiting templates
- How long is the relocation stipend valid? -> 90 days from start date unless otherwise stated

B. Ownership matrix (high-level)
| Process step | Owner | Secondary | SLA |
| --- | --- | --- | ---: |
| Requisition approval | Hiring manager + Finance | People Ops | 3 business days |
| Posting & sourcing | Recruiting | Hiring manager | 2 business days to post |
| Background checks | People Ops | Recruiting | Initiate within 24 hours of verbal acceptance |
| Equipment procurement | Recruiting / Ops | Manager | 2 business days to order |

C. Links & resources
- Recruiting playbook (Greenhouse): /confluence/recruiting/playbook
- Manager interview training: /confluence/learning/interviewer-training
- People Ops forms & templates: /confluence/company-handbook/people-ops-forms
